tasks.description: RAISED BY T159, WHICH FOUND IT BY DETONATING IT rather than by reading. The shared Java capture rig -- inherited by T83, T84, T100 AND T117 alike -- catches RuntimeException, not Throwable. A java.lang.StackOverflowError is an Error, NOT a RuntimeException, so it is precisely what slips through, AND T159 OBSERVED EXACTLY THAT: two cells died with java.lang.StackOverflowError from ProgressiveEMICalculator.calculateLastUnpaidRepaymentPeriodEMI recursing into itself at ProgressiveEMICalculator.java:1214, non-monotonically -- (B=10001,n=2000) dies while (B=10001,n=3000) succeeds. With this hole, '0 errored' is consistent with BOTH 'nothing failed' AND 'the failures were invisible to the handler' -- the P-40 class (an enumerator that cannot see what it skipped) reaching the ERROR path instead of the enumeration path. Fix: catch Throwable, record the throwable's class and message as a FIRST-CLASS OUTCOME distinct from both success and absence, and make the integrity line report it -- 'N asked / N observed / N threw / N skipped'. A cell that threw is NOT an observation and must never be graded as one, and must never be silently absent either.
